title: Leading Open AI Models Now Available in Model Vault | Cohere
gist: Cohere launches third-party open models (DeepSeek, GLM, MiMo, Gemma, Nemotron, GPT-OSS, Phi, Hy3) inside its single-tenant Model Vault and confidential-computing Model Vault Encrypted, pitching 'sovereign inference' to regulated enterprises. Encrypted currently supports only a subset of models and is US-only, with EU and Canada coming.

insights.claim: Cohere defines sovereign inference as customer control over four things: where data lives, who can access it, which models can be used, and how the AI runs rather than the provider dictating it.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is framing data residency and model choice as the enterprise buying criteria against hyperscaler shared APIs.

insights.claim: Banks, hospitals and government departments often cannot send sensitive data to a shared API, yet may lack the capacity to run open or on-premise models themselves, forcing a tradeoff between desired model, needed control and manageable capacity.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Names the unmet demand for managed-but-isolated inference in regulated sectors that Cohere targets.
insights.locator: Every organization wants to use the best AI models

insights.claim: Cohere argues no single model is best at everything, so enterprises want to pick the right model per task while keeping the same protections across all of them.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Multi-model neutrality is used as a differentiator versus single-provider platforms.
insights.quote: No single model is best at everything.
insights.locator: The right model for every job

insights.claim: Cohere casts freedom of model choice as something that should never come at the expense of security or privacy, positioning Model Vault as vendor-neutral in model choice.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Signals Cohere is pivoting from pure model vendor toward neutral secure hosting platform.

insights.claim: Model Vault runs workloads on single-tenant infrastructure in a region the customer chooses, with Cohere managing the cluster so customers avoid building their own serving stack.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Managed isolated tenancy is the baseline offering to compete with self-hosting.
insights.locator: Model Vault: Your models and workloads

insights.claim: Model Vault Encrypted uses confidential computing so prompts and outputs stay encrypted during processing, with neither Cohere nor any cloud provider able to see them.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Protecting data in use is the premium tier for the most sensitive workloads and a potential moat in regulated AI.
insights.locator: Model Vault Encrypted: For your most sensitive work

insights.claim: Zero data retention of prompts and outputs is the default in Model Vault.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Table-stakes security claim for enterprise inference buyers.

insights.claim: Model Vault Encrypted currently supports only some models: Cohere's Embed, Rerank, Parse, Transcribe and Translate plus Gemma, GPT-OSS and Phi, while Command, DeepSeek, GLM, MiMo, Nemotron and Hy3 are not yet supported there.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Confidential compute is still limited, notably excluding Cohere's flagship Command generative model and most large open models.

insights.claim: Cohere plans larger models in Model Vault Encrypted, indicating confidential compute currently cannot handle more demanding workloads.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Confidential-computing overhead or capacity limits constrain model size today.

insights.claim: Model Vault hosts models from many developers: Cohere, DeepSeek, Z.ai (GLM), Xiaomi (MiMo), Google (Gemma), NVIDIA (Nemotron), OpenAI (GPT-OSS), Microsoft (Phi) and Tencent (Hy3).
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Shows how many Chinese and US open-weight models are now being offered via Western enterprise platforms.

insights.claim: Cohere describes DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the most-used open model on OpenRouter.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Usage data point suggesting Chinese open models lead open-weight adoption among developers.
insights.quote: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (the most-used open model on OpenRouter)

insights.claim: Cohere expects to add more models in every region as new open models are released and adopted, committing to follow the open-model release cycle.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Hosting layer value depends on keeping pace with open-model churn.

insights.claim: Model Vault is live in the United States, European Union and Canada, while Model Vault Encrypted is live only in the US with EU and Canada coming soon.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Regional gaps in the encrypted tier limit near-term EU and Canadian regulated adoption.

insights.claim: Model Vault pricing is by GPU type with on-demand hourly rates, and reserved capacity with monthly and annual commits via sales.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: GPU-hour pricing makes this an infrastructure-style business rather than per-token API revenue.

insights.claim: RWS's Language Weaver uses Model Vault to run models including its LW Pro model, citing zero data retention, data residency and Cohere handling hosting and scaling.
insights.speaker: Dragos Munteanu, VP Research and Product Development, RWS
insights.so_what: Named customer reference showing demand from translation vendors handling sensitive content.
insights.quote: Cohere handles the hosting and scaling, our teams can stay focused on what we do best
